correctness.rationale: A direct induction establishes distance-two exclusion as equivalent to total visibility on Hamming graphs; a four-label parity and column argument classifies every face for n>=2. Two joins of n zero-spheres with 4n explicit bridging edges give the claimed integral wedge homotopy. Counting and token-jumping are derived explicitly; a standard-library verifier independently checks n=2..6, including direct all-pairs path testing for n=2,3 and chain boundary ranks for n<=4. No finite test is used to justify the unrestricted result.

value.rationale: Total mutual-visibility sets naturally form a hereditary simplicial complex. In the first thin three-factor Hamming family, this complex exhibits a complete nonpure facet spectrum with arbitrarily long missing facet sizes, an exact two-sphere plus many-circle integral homotopy, and a sharp token-jumping connectivity transition. These interconnected answers go beyond the previously known maximum number n and provide a concrete infinite family relating geodesic visibility, combinatorial topology, and reconfiguration.
